label: MiCA Crypto-Asset Classification
description: Classify a crypto-asset under MiCA (EU) 2023/1114 — e-money token (EMT), asset-referenced token (ART), other crypto-asset, or out-of-scope. Test against the significant-token thresholds, map the EMD2 interface for EMTs, and derive the issuer obligations that follow each class.

claudeKnowledge.description: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA) Titles III, IV and Annexes; Directive 2009/110/EC (EMD2); Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 (TFR); EBA and ESMA MiCA Level 2/3 measures (RTS/ITS/guidelines on classification, significance, white papers, own funds); ESMA classification guidelines under Art. 97 MiCA.

guidedInputs.label: Crypto-Asset Profile
guidedInputs.description: Which description best fits the value-stabilisation design of the asset?

options.label: Pegged 1:1 to a single official currency (e.g. EUR or USD)
References a basket of official currencies
References commodities, other crypto-assets, or a mixed basket
Algorithmic / no reserve backing the stabilisation mechanism
Provides access to a good/service on a DLT network (utility)

guidedInputs.label: Your Role / Entity Type
guidedInputs.description: From whose perspective is the classification being run? This drives which authorisation and obligations follow.

options.label: Crypto-asset service provider (CASP) seeking to offer/admit
New issuer / project team (offeror seeking authorisation)
Adviser / counsel assessing on behalf of a client

guidedInputs.label: Home / Relevant Jurisdiction(s)
guidedInputs.description: Which competent authorities are relevant for authorisation and the white-paper notification?

guidedInputs.label: Significance Indicators (if known)
guidedInputs.description: Tick any threshold the asset is approaching or expected to exceed — these drive the significant-EMT / significant-ART assessment and EBA supervision.

options.label: Issue value / reserve above EUR 5 billion
More than 2.5 million transactions / EUR 500m daily
Issuer also issues other ARTs/EMTs or provides CASP services

guidedInputs.label: Asset Design & Known Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe the redemption mechanism, reserve composition, par-value claim, rights conferred to holders, distribution channels, and any classification doubts or supervisory feedback received.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Token is redeemable at par in EUR on demand; reserve held in segregated bank deposits and short-dated EU sovereign bonds; holders have a direct claim on the issuer; uncertain whether the 'rewards' feature creates an interest-bearing characteristic prohibited under MiCA Art. 50...

exampleInput: We are a Swedish EMI planning to issue 'NordEUR', a token redeemable 1:1 in euro on demand, fully backed by segregated EUR bank deposits and short-dated EU sovereign bonds. We expect distribution across the Nordics and Germany via two partner CASPs, and we project crossing 10 million holders and EUR 5 billion in issuance within 18 months. Classify NordEUR under MiCA, confirm whether it is an EMT or an ART, walk us through the EMD2 interface and the par-value/redemption-at-any-moment and no-interest rules, test it against the significant-EMT thresholds, and set out the issuer obligations and white-paper / authorisation path that follow. We also offer holders a small loyalty reward for holding the token — flag any conflict with the no-interest prohibition.

exampleValues.design_details: Token redeemable 1:1 in EUR on demand. Reserve = segregated EUR bank deposits + short-dated EU sovereign bonds. Holders have a direct legal claim on the issuer at par. Distribution via two partner CASPs across the Nordics and Germany. A loyalty 'reward' accrues to holders the longer they hold — need confirmation this does not breach the MiCA no-interest prohibition for EMTs.
